comments.message: This introduces a persisted table without a matching Alembic revision. `alembic upgrade head` still tops out before `personal_access_tokens`, so non-dev databases will never get this table and both `/api/v1/auth/tokens` and PAT-backed `/mcp` auth will fail after deployment.

PAT verification only checks the token row and `revoked_at`. It never verifies that the owning user is still active, so a deactivated account keeps MCP access through previously issued personal access tokens until each token is manually revoked.

This assertion is too weak to protect the new MCP path: `/mcp/` returning 404, 405, or 500 still passes as long as it is not `401`. Assert the expected successful/allowed status so the test actually catches broken PAT-authenticated MCP routing.
